resources.string: Your keyholder uses Google Authenticator, or a compatible authenticator app, on their own phone. It generates short-lived codes that they can share with you from anywhere.
Remove this keyholder? Their codes will stop opening your locks. Your Dom PIN will still work.
Ask your keyholder to scan this with Google Authenticator or another authenticator app on their phone.
Enter the displayed key manually in your authenticator.
Key handed over. Their next fresh code can open your locks.
Code expired, already used, or incorrect. Check automatic time on both phones and try a fresh code.
Too many attempts. Wait before trying another code, or use the Dom PIN.
Authenticator unavailable. Use the Dom PIN to pair it again.

Choose a fixed duration or agree to a random time within the range below. The duration is chosen once when the Pact starts. Hiding the countdown conceals it in Sub mode; the controller can still inspect it.
Use an ordered range between 0.5 and 720 hours.
A Pact is already active, or the new Pact could not be saved.
Your keyholder has the setup key in Google Authenticator or their chosen authenticator. Ask them for the current six-digit code when you need Dom access.
A little trust. One little key.
Your keyholder adds the QR code or manual setup key to Google Authenticator (or a compatible app). They do not need SubHub.
Their authenticator generates a new six-digit code every 30 seconds. Ask them to share the current code when they approve access.
Choose Keyholder code at a Dom prompt and enter the code before it expires. It opens the same controls as the PIN.
No timed Pact is active. Choose your lock on Home, then enter service when you are ready.
Choose the way that fits your arrangement. PIN and authenticator both open the same Dom controls; codes do not send remote commands.
Ask your keyholder for the code showing in their authenticator.
Nothing changes until you confirm. Keep the pairing key private.
